Hunting, weapons and animals

Hunting is one of the two renewable food sources in survival; the other is fishing. No animal fights back, so the only hard part is getting close enough and keeping the weapon ready.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 4 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides
Contents
  1. Animals are passive
  2. Hit with a hand, tool or sword
  3. Throwing rocks
  4. Alder bow and arrows
  5. Alder rifle
  6. What you get from a kill
  7. How this was checked

Animals are passive

Every animal is passive. None of them attack, chase or damage you. Farm animals stay calm near you; cows, sheep, pigs and chickens drift in loose groups and stand still through the night. Small wild animals, such as rabbits and foxes, keep their distance and run when you come close. Any animal runs for a few seconds after you hurt it. Peaceful world: no hostile mobs Animal behaviour

Good to know. There is no taming, riding, breeding, feeding, milking or shearing.

Hit with a hand, tool or sword

  1. Aim at the animal from within 6 m.
  2. Left-click to hit it.
  3. A hurt animal runs off for a few seconds. Chase it and hit it again.

An empty hand, a held block or a Stone pickaxe, hatchet or shovel deals 12 damage. The Stone sword deals 28. Rabbits and chickens fall to one hit, pigs, sheep and goats to one sword hit, deer and wolves to two. A cow takes two sword hits, or five bare-handed. In creative, one hit removes the animal and gives you nothing. Tall grass or flowers between you and the animal can block the hit. Hitting animals (melee)

Tools & arms 1 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Stone sword1 Stone sword
  • 4× Natural stone (any of 26 natural stones; mixable)
  • 2× Boards of any species (mixable)

Crafted tools are equipped automatically.

Good to know. With a bow, rocks, a fishing rod or the furniture hammer in hand, left click does not hit animals in survival. Put it away or equip a stone tool.

A struck animal yelps, and a kill ends with a short sigh. The 57 animals with voices do this; quiet ones, such as fish, insects and rabbits, make only the hit thud. See Creatures.

Throwing rocks

Key or actionWhat it does
Hold right clickWind up. A full wind-up takes 0.7 s.
Release right clickThrow. A wind-up that is too short is cancelled.

Harder throws fly farther and hit harder: a full wind-up deals 20 damage, a half wind-up a quarter of that. Each throw uses one rock in survival. A throw that cannot fly, such as one with no valid aim, keeps the rock. Rocks hurt animals only, not you or vehicles, and fly through grass and flowers. Throwing rocks

Tools & arms 1 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Four throwing rocks4 Throwing rock
  • 4× Natural stone (any of 26 natural stones; mixable)

Each Throwing rock weighs 0.6 kg versus 0.125 kg per stone piece, so crafting rocks raises carried mass.

Alder bow and arrows

  1. Craft an Alder bow and some arrows.
  2. Equip the bow. Press Tab or Shift + Tab to cycle through what you carry.
  3. Hold right click to draw. A full draw takes 0.85 s.
  4. Release to shoot. Letting go before about a fifth of a draw cancels the shot.
Key or actionWhat it does
Hold right click, releaseDraw and shoot.
Hold ShiftSneak to steady your aim.

Longer draws fly faster and hit harder: a full draw deals 30 damage, a half draw a quarter of that. A DRAW gauge fills while you hold. In survival each shot uses one arrow, and arrows are not recovered. A shot that cannot fly, such as one with no valid aim, keeps the arrow. Arrows fly through grass, flowers and other soft ground plants, but stop on turf, trunks, leaves, buildings and furniture. An arrow that lands in leaves makes a soft rustle. Other impacts make a thunk that fades out by about 48 m. Creative arrows are unlimited. Alder bow and arrows

Alder rifle

Key or actionWhat it does
Left clickFire.
Hold right clickRaise the sights for less spread and sway. You cannot aim while it reloads.
Hold ShiftSneak to steady your aim.
RDoes not reload the rifle. In survival, R eats food instead.

The rifle reloads itself about one second after every shot, and a RELOAD gauge shows it. Each round deals 44 damage. Survival uses one rifle round per shot; creative is unlimited. A shot that cannot fly keeps its round. Rounds hurt animals and vehicles and, like arrows, fly through grass and flowers. Alder rifle and rifle rounds

What you get from a kill

In survival, a killed animal leaves its drops on the ground where it fell, and the status line reads 'Defeated … | collect the dropped items'. After about a second, walk up to them to pick up what fits in your pack; anything that does not fit stays on the ground until you make room. Creative kills give nothing. If the drops would have no clear spot to land, the killing blow is refused ('Animal kept') and the animal survives. Animal drops

Key or actionWhat it does
Cow3 Raw meat, 2 Hide
Pig3 Raw meat
Sheep2 Raw meat, 3 Wool
Chicken1 Raw meat, 3 Feathers
Deer3 Venison, 1 Hide (the only Venison)
Rabbit, duck, goose, frog, fish1 Raw meat
Goat, boar, horse, zebra2 Raw meat, 1 Hide
Wolf, lion, tiger2 Raw meat, 2 Hide
Fox1 Hide only

Other mammals drop 1 to 3 Raw meat and 1 to 2 Hide, and other birds 1 or 2 Raw meat and 2 Feathers. Whales and elephants give meat only, and butterflies, flies, bats, hummingbirds and other tiny animals drop nothing. Meat and venison are food, feathers make arrows, and wool can replace plant fiber. Hide has no use yet.

Fire & food 3 recipes
RecipeMakesNeeds
Burn a charcoal pile2 Charcoal
  • 4× Boards of any species (mixable)
Cook raw meat1 Cooked meat
  • 1× Raw meat
  • 1× Charcoal

Raw meat restores 8 hunger, Cooked meat 30. A placed cooking stove cooks the same recipe.

Roast venison2 Cooked meat
  • 1× Venison
  • 1× Charcoal

One Venison (18 hunger raw) becomes 2 Cooked meat (30 each). A placed cooking stove cooks the same recipe.

Cook meat with Charcoal before you eat it: craft it on the Craft tab, or cook it on a placed cooking stove. Cooked meat restores 30 hunger against 8 for Raw meat, and Venison roasts into two. See Your first survival day for the other hunger numbers.

How this guide was checked

Controls, damage, draw times and drop rules come from the game source at the audited commit. Each ledger entry lists its source lines. Re-checked at Voxelgame 21d656c2d5c32e82fd6287804078f391ef930657 on 8 November 2026, beneath crates/voxelgame-core/src/: melee reach, damage and refusals (game/creature_melee.rs, session/creatures.rs, inventory.rs), throw, draw and rifle input and damage (game/ranged_input.rs, game/readouts.rs, projectile.rs, projectile/rifles.rs), shots passing soft plants (world/raycast.rs), kills, loot and the drop table (entities/melee.rs, entities/species_profile.rs, game/item_drops.rs, dropped_items.rs), animal behaviour (entities/mod.rs, entities/idle_behaviour.rs), and the hurt and death cries (game/audio.rs, events.rs and src/audio/effects.rs in the game root). The cooking advice in 'What you get from a kill' was first re-checked at Voxelgame dfeb362ddeca56ff5de77fa26ccdb6e37d05192c on 8 November 2026, and the drop rules at Voxelgame 251b9e46aeefd207a5e34046dd8a973c2a2cb480 on the same day.

Initial ledger audit: Voxelgame main dd29d91, committed 10 October 2026; article updated 8 November 2026. Source-checked at Voxelgame 21d656c2 on 8 November 2026; not play-tested. Draw, wind-up and reload times are the code values; check them in play if they feel different. The hit counts come from the animals' health and the damage numbers, not from play. The bow, rocks and rifle on a server were not re-read at 21d656c2.
